notes: The Hotel Zone R1/R2 bus costs 15 MXN; ADO buses go to Chichén, Tulum and Playa. A rental car gives you freedom for the cenotes (insurance is expensive).

June-November is hurricane season (peak August-October). Expect 33°C, high humidity and afternoon downpours. Sargassum (seaweed) can hit beaches from May to August; Isla Mujeres' Playa Norte stays clean.
Arrive at Chichén Itzá and Tulum for the 08:00 opening; by noon it's 35°C and the tour buses arrive. Non-biodegradable sunscreen is banned in cenotes.
Hotel Zone restaurants cost 3-5 times more; Mercado 28 and the centre (Parque de las Palapas) have local prices. Pay in pesos; the dollar rate is poor.
Tip 10-15%; say "no gracias" to beach vendors. Drink bottled water.
Ferries: Isla Mujeres from Puerto Juárez (Hotel Zone piers are pricey), Cozumel from Playa, Holbox from Chiquilá.

stops.name: Playa Delfines
stops.tips: Cancún's biggest free beach: no hotels, turquoise Caribbean water. Check for sargassum season (May-August).

stops.name: Cancún Sign Playa Delfines
stops.tips: Colourful CANCUN letters, a good photo stop.

stops.name: El Fish Fritanga
stops.tips: Local fish restaurant on the lagoon shore. Try the ceviche and tikin xic (Yucatán grilled fish); rare cheap eats for the Hotel Zone.

stops.name: Museo Maya de Cancún
stops.tips: Maya museum with the San Miguelito ruins; an air-conditioned afternoon option.

stops.name: Playa Chac Mool
stops.tips: Central public beach for sunset and waves.

backups.name: Mercado 28 Los De Pescado
backups.tips: Fish tacos in the downtown market, a spot for locals.

backups.name: Playa Tortugas
backups.tips: Calm beach on the lagoon side, next to the ferry pier.

stops.name: Ultramar Ferry Puerto Juárez
stops.tips: 20-minute ferry (about 28 USD return). Rent a golf cart on the island (about 800 MXN).

stops.name: Playa Norte
stops.tips: One of the world's best beaches: shallow and calm, sun loungers 100-200 MXN.

stops.name: Punta Sur Isla Mujeres
stops.tips: The island's southern tip, with the Ixchel temple ruins and a sculpture park. The first sunrise in Mexico.

stops.name: Mango Cafe Isla Mujeres
stops.tips: Caribbean breakfast and lunch; the coconut French toast is the island's famous dish.

stops.name: MUSA Underwater Museum Snorkelling
stops.tips: 500 underwater sculptures. Snorkel tours leave from the pier; take the 17:30 ferry back.

backups.name: Isla Mujeres Mercado Municipal
backups.tips: Cheap local food at the municipal market.

backups.name: Garrafón Reef Park
backups.tips: Zipline and snorkelling park, an alternative to MUSA.

stops.name: Chichén Itzá
stops.tips: 2.5 hours from Cancún (ADO bus or tour). See the Kukulkan pyramid and ball court; it's cool and empty at the 08:00 opening. Entry about 697 MXN.

stops.name: Cenote Ik Kil
stops.tips: 5 minutes from Chichén. An open cenote 26 m deep with hanging vines; life jackets are compulsory.

stops.name: Casa Tía Micha Valladolid
stops.tips: Yucatán cuisine in Valladolid: try the cochinita pibil (slow-roast pork) and sopa de lima (lime soup).

stops.name: Calzada de los Frailes Valladolid
stops.tips: A pastel-coloured colonial street leading to the Convent of San Bernardino.

stops.name: Cenote Suytun
stops.tips: Cave cenote with a beam of light. Visit in the afternoon for the light; the drive back takes 2 hours.

backups.name: Cenote Zací Valladolid
backups.tips: A cenote in the town, instead of Suytun.

backups.name: El Mesón del Marqués Valladolid
backups.tips: Colonial restaurant on the main square.

stops.name: Tulum Ruins
stops.tips: 2 hours from Cancún. A Maya fortress by the sea, opening at 08:00. Entry about 95 MXN plus parking, and look out for iguanas.

stops.name: Playa Ruinas Tulum
stops.tips: The beach below the ruins, good for a short swim.

stops.name: Gran Cenote
stops.tips: Cave cenote for snorkelling, with turtles and stalactites. The water is clearest in the morning.

stops.name: Taquería Honorio Tulum
stops.tips: Tulum's legendary breakfast and lunch taco spot. Try the cochinita and lechón (suckling pig); it closes when the food runs out at 14:00.

stops.name: Tulum Beach Road
stops.tips: Palm-lined coastal road. Choose a beach club (Papaya Playa) or a public beach (Playa Paraíso).

backups.name: Cenote Dos Ojos
backups.tips: A cave system with two "eyes", instead of Gran Cenote.

backups.name: Antojitos La Chiapaneca
backups.tips: Al pastor in Tulum town, for the evening.

stops.name: Xel-Há Park
stops.tips: A huge natural aquarium cove with unlimited snorkelling and buffet (about 110 USD). You can swim even in the rain.

stops.name: Xel-Há Buffet
stops.tips: Unlimited buffet included.

stops.name: Quinta Avenida Playa del Carmen
stops.tips: Playa del Carmen's pedestrian street, for an evening walk and mezcal.

backups.name: Cenote Azul
backups.tips: Open cenote by the roadside, a cheap alternative to Xel-Há.

backups.name: El Fogón Playa del Carmen
backups.tips: Al pastor tacos in Playa, instead of the park.

stops.name: Cozumel Ferry Playa del Carmen
stops.tips: 45-minute ferry from Playa (about 500 MXN return). The Caribbean's best diving island.

stops.name: Palancar Reef Snorkelling
stops.tips: Cozumel's famous reef. Take a boat tour to see turtles and coral.

stops.name: Casa Mission Cozumel
stops.tips: Mexican-Maya cuisine on Cozumel.

stops.name: Punta Sur Eco Park Cozumel
stops.tips: Lighthouse and crocodile lagoon; you'll need a rental vehicle.

backups.name: Isla Contoy Tour
backups.tips: Bird island with snorkelling off Isla Mujeres, instead of Holbox or Cozumel.

stops.name: Mercado 28
stops.tips: Downtown handicraft market for hammocks and silver. Haggle 40% off.

stops.name: Cocina La Chaya Mercado 28
stops.tips: Yucatán home cooking: panuchos (filled fried tortillas) and chaya juice, a farewell meal.

stops.name: Parque de las Palapas
stops.tips: Downtown square. Marquesitas (crispy crepes) stalls open in the evening; it's quiet by day.

stops.name: ADO Airport Bus
stops.tips: ADO bus from the centre to the airport takes 30 minutes.

backups.name: Taquería Los Charros Cancún
backups.tips: Tacos downtown, instead of the market.

backups.name: Playa Langosta
backups.tips: One last swim in the Hotel Zone.
